instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the minced onion and grated carrots and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until soft.
Add the garlic, oregano, mint and pepper. Stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the stock and 1 cup of water. Turn the heat to high, cover, and bring it to a boil. That takes about 7 minutes.
Meanwhile, pull the meat off the rotisserie chicken and shred 2 cups of it. Set it aside.
Break the vermicelli into short pieces. Add it to the boiling soup and cook for 5 minutes, stirring once or twice, until tender.
In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, the juice of the lemon and the egg yolk until smooth. Whisk in a ladleful of hot broth, then a second ladleful.
Turn the heat to low. Pour the lemon mixture into the pot, stirring as you pour. Simmer gently for 3 minutes, until the soup thickens slightly. Don't let it boil hard.
Add the shredded chicken and cook for 2 minutes, until it's warm.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the chopped parsley.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with crusty bread. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat them over low heat, stirring, and don't let the soup boil.
method_notes: This follows Little Spice Jar's soup: onion and carrot softened first, then herbs, stock and vermicelli, finished with a flour, lemon and egg yolk mix stirred in at the end. Little Spice Jar (5 out of 5 from 8 votes, so below the 20 ratings needed) uses butter and Greek yogurt in that mix; both are left out here to keep it dairy-free, and olive oil replaces the butter. Cup of Yum's version also cooks in oil and finishes with lemon and parsley or dill. Written with rotisserie chicken to keep it near 30 minutes.
